author: /root/character_surgery_repair
scope: NEW constructive smooth Morse-compatible disk w-region and ribbon TREE spine. Not a mathematical review or extension of any accepted repaired supplier; no canonical changes/checks.
input: An actual smooth oriented connected genus-g surface F⊂S3×I from a doubly pointed unknot to a doubly pointed knot, with two product-collared boundary circles, and a chosen finite Morse movie for the height h|F with distinct interior critical values. The endpoint w-intervals are fixed. This construction is relative to that actual movie; it does not replace the embedded surface by an abstract2g-saddle word.
claim: There is an embedded finite ribbon tree T⊂F with exactly two leaves on∂F (in the chosen endpoint w-intervals), all other vertices/leaves interior, and a smoothly rounded disk neighborhood W⊂F which meets∂F precisely in those endpoint intervals. For every level regular for both the surface movie and dividing boundary, every intermediate link component has a nonempty open w-interval in W and a nonempty open z-interval in Z=closure(F−W). The critical surface saddles can lie entirely in Z; birth/death critical points lie on the smooth dividing boundary, with the explicit local mixed-color cap below. Z is connected genusg with one boundary and chi1−2g. No claim that T is ambiently isotopic to a bare arc or that its graph map is the identity is made.

actual_construction_and_proof.label: Finite regular tracks
actual_construction_and_proof.argument: Choose disjoint small critical-value intervals and compact regular slabs between them. On a regular slab use the smooth vector field grad(h)/|grad(h)|², which has dh(V)=1. Its flow exists across that compact slab and identifies each component with a circle times the height interval. There are finitely many such circle components. Choose a short angular interval in each circle and one vertical core track through it; also choose a disjoint nearby vertical trace to remain protected z. All tracks are compact arcs with endpoints in the interior of F. Endpoint product collars retain their chosen w- and z-intervals. No whole level circle is selected as a track.

actual_construction_and_proof.label: Birth/death cap with both colors
actual_construction_and_proof.argument: At a surface birth use Morse coordinates h−c=x²+y² on a disk. Choose0<delta sufficiently small and let the local w-cap be the closed disk B_delta given x²+(y−delta)²≤delta². Its boundary is smooth and passes through the critical point p=(0,0), whereas its center (0,delta) will be an interior leaf of T. On a level circle x²+y²=r², membership is y≥r²/(2delta). For every0<r<2delta this contains a nonempty open upper arc, while the lower arc y<0 lies outside. Thus the newborn circle has BOTH colors at every sufficiently small positive regular level; the critical point is not hidden in the interior of a monochromatic w-disk. Attach a narrow outward radial strip along the positive y-axis from the cap center into the adjacent regular cylinder; choose it so that W intersects all remaining radii up to that slab. Protect a negative-y trace in Z. The same construction at a death uses c−h=x²+y². The cap boundary passes through p as a smooth dividing arc; locally y=x²/(2delta)+higher terms. Subsequent connecting paths stay outside this critical disk except at the chosen outward port, so they cannot destroy the protected opposite-color arc.

actual_construction_and_proof.label: Saddle neighborhoods
actual_construction_and_proof.argument: At a saddle use h−c=x²−y². Choose a small fixed a>0 and eta<a²/2. In the four regular arms take the four disjoint tracks x=±a,y=±sqrt(a²−t), with t=h−c in[−eta,eta]. Each is a regular height-parametrized arc, and none passes through the critical point. Every local level branch entering or leaving the saddle disk passes a regular arm; taking the critical disk and eta small makes these tracks meet all incident global link components. Place a disjoint nearby protected z-trace in each arm. All other link components through the interval are regular cylinders treated as in step1. The w-tracks avoid a smaller disk about the saddle point, so the surface saddle itself remains in Z, giving a z-region saddle rather than an assumed global all-z movie.

actual_construction_and_proof.label: No forced joins or cycles
actual_construction_and_proof.argument: Choose tracks in overlap collars as disjoint parallel arcs, not as identified endpoints. This makes the complete finite set of regular tracks, local radial tracks and cap-center leaves a disjoint finite forest in the interior of F. Overlapping HEIGHT ranges ensure coverage of intermediate components without requiring spatial intersections or endpoint gluings. The protected z-traces are another disjoint interior forest. Local critical caps are fixed and avoided except at their outward ports. Thus no cycle is forced by a cycle in the Reeb graph of the movie: the selected tracks are not a graph section of that Reeb graph.

actual_construction_and_proof.label: Connect the forest to a tree
actual_construction_and_proof.argument: First choose a simple proper root arc joining the two endpoint w-intervals, avoiding the interior track forest, protected z-traces and fixed cap interiors. A finite collection of disjoint compact interior arcs and disks does not disconnect a connected surface: a transverse path can be detoured around either interior endpoint of each arc or around the boundary of each disk. A proper arc joining different boundary components is nonseparating, by the boundary detour argument recorded in the disk-spine report. With that root arc installed, the complement of it and the remaining interior forest is still connected. Attach one remaining forest component at a time by a simple smooth bridge with interior disjoint from the current tree, the other forest components, protected z-traces and fixed cap interiors. The bridge meets exactly one point of each of TWO DIFFERENT components. Consequently it joins components and never adds a cycle. Smooth or declare a trivalent ribbon vertex at each attachment, preserving all cap ports. Finite induction produces a connected acyclic embedded graph T. Only the original two root endpoints lie on∂F; all additional leaves are interior.

actual_construction_and_proof.label: Choose neighborhood without losing z-intervals
actual_construction_and_proof.argument: Thicken T in the oriented surface, using the fixed tangent caps from step2, narrow strips along its edges and small vertex disks. At each vertex the incident cyclic order is the actual order of the tangent half-edges in the orientation of F; it is retained by the thickening, not chosen arbitrarily. A regular neighborhood of a finite tree is a disk: start with its vertex disks and add edge rectangles in a leaf-first order, each connecting two distinct already-disjoint disk components, so each addition preserves a disk component and creates no handle. The resulting W meets∂F in exactly the two prescribed endpoint intervals. On compact regular slabs, a level circle cannot be contained in T because a tree contains no embedded circle. The maximum distance of that circle from T is positive and varies continuously under the explicit flow trivialization; its minimum over the compact slab is positive. Choose the strip/vertex radii smaller than this bound and small enough to avoid the protected z-traces. Every component still meets a prescribed w-track, hence W, and also retains an open interval outside W. In the birth/death neighborhoods the fixed cap calculation and protected opposite trace give both colors directly; at saddles the arm w/z traces do so. Round corners away from the fixed tangency germs and protected traces, keeping these strict inclusions. This supplies alternating nonempty w/z intervals at every joint regular level. Additional critical levels of h on the dividing boundary are allowed marked-point/quasi-stabilization events, not silently discarded.

actual_construction_and_proof.label: Complement and genus
actual_construction_and_proof.argument: The root arc joins distinct boundary components and has connected complement. Adding an attached interior tree branch only adds a finger ending at an interior leaf; the two sides of that finger reconnect around its endpoint, so complement connectedness is preserved inductively. The same holds after thickening. Thus Z is connected. The boundary of W has precisely two endpoint intervals on∂F and otherwise two dividing arcs, so removing W merges the two old boundary circles into one boundary circle of Z. Since W∩Z is the pair of dividing intervals, chi(F)=chi(W)+chi(Z)−2 gives−2g=1+chi(Z)−2 and chi(Z)=1−2g. The connected orientable surface Z with one boundary component therefore has genusg.

map_theoretic_limits: T generally has trivalent ribbon vertices and interior leaves. It is NOT a bare proper arc. The accepted codimension-three bare-arc theorem cannot collapse those vertices/leaves, and is not invoked for this new tree.

The actual graph map of T still needs local ribbon-leaf/trivalent birth/death cancellation, cyclic-order-sensitive graph action, and the finite graph-word comparison to the surface movie. Topological contractibility alone does not prove a unit Floer action.

The actual arbitrary-old-factor edge/quasi-stabilization operations and forget-z adjacent-edge identities newly authored by the Floer owners may be used at their supplied extent. This geometry report neither rechecks those operations nor extends their scope to an unproved whole movie-to-graph theorem.

The available strict S−A_lambda S+=Id relation normalizes a paired free-basepoint subdivision word. A separate dictionary must identify which leaf/trivalent graph moves have that word. No arbitrary tree reduction is inferred from a two-generator scalar calculation.

chi(W)=1,chi(Z)=1−2g give the target region values only. Absolute Maslov shift0 follows IF an actual homogeneous end map sends normalized tower1→1. Alexander shiftg still requires the actual relativeSeifert/Euler degree operation; no degree formula is proved merely by Euler arithmetic.

Once actual graph normalization and marked surface degree operations produce F:R→A_g,tower1→1, the saved/frozen original-facing Vs/Hs proof yields nu-minus≤g.
